title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer regional failover thresholds to avoid thrashing
author: Riley Chen
description:
Motivation: After the incident on 2026-02-19 we observed repeated regional failover thrashing from the SLO enforcer when transient latency spikes coincided with aggressive backoff parameters. This PR tightens the regional failover thresholds and adds additional hysteresis to reduce failover churn while preserving SLO enforcement.

What I changed: single continuous description containing checklist and details. Adjusted the enforcer to require sustained breach windows, increased the backoff multiplier floor, and added an explicit minimum cool-down per-region to avoid immediate re-triggering. Also added unit tests and an integration test for simulated transient spikes.

Changes: 1) config: default regional_failover.window_seconds from 30 -> 90, 2) config: regional_failover.cooldown_seconds set to 120 (was 0), 3) enforcer: require consecutive_breach_count >= 3 within window to mark region as degraded, 4) backoff: clamp multiplier to [1.25, 5.0] instead of [1.0, 10.0], 5) metrics: new metric slo_enforcer.failover_decision_reason with tags for diagnostics.

Checklist:
- [x] Reproduced thrashing locally with workload harness
- [x] Added unit tests for breach window logic
- [x] Added integration test in perf-canary simulating transient spikes
- [x] Updated docs snippet in redwood-docs explaining new config knobs
- [x] Deployed to staging and ran canary for 24h
- [x] Rollback plan: revert config change or set window_seconds back to 30

Linear: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3784/tighten-slo-enforcer-thresholds
Related: ENG-3790 (observability for failover diagnostics).
